fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10, whereas the target study designed an as-cast Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloy using equimolar NbMoTaVW as the baseline.

It replaces the target intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation followed by VEC/modulus/density screening of 38,326 compositions—with an unimplemented physics-informed multi-fidelity machine-learning framework.
It proposes tensile and fracture-toughness prediction, while the decisive target experiment was room-temperature quasi-static compression and did not report fracture toughness.
The claimed 15–20% accuracy improvement and greater than 80% computational-cost reduction are unsupported by the cited evidence.

The cited papers provide only broad motivation for advanced alloy design and computational screening; they do not validate the proposed model, descriptors, quantitative gains, or application to HfNbTiVAl10.
The falsification threshold is not operationally defined because the comparator models, error metric, dataset split, sample count, and computational-cost accounting are unspecified.
explanation: The generated hypothesis is a generic prospective ML proposal rather than a reconstruction of the target work. It misses the alloy system, composition-screening strategy, VEC-based dislocation-mobility rationale, as-cast BCC structural mediator, compression conditions, and measured outcome of 35.7% fracture strain at 1115 MPa yield strength. Its out-of-distribution boundary is reasonable in general, and a blinded test is suggested, but the benchmark lacks fixed protocols and preregistered metrics. The evidence supports only the broad need for efficient HEA-design tools, not the specific architecture or numerical performance claims.
